match.reason: No bank point teaches the business cycle at Stage 5 depth: the closest, eco-business-cycle, is a Year 12 Economics card built on real GDP, trend lines and growth rates, which is too deep and too macro for this Commerce brief about how businesses adjust to booms and recessions.

draft.title: The business cycle
card: The business cycle is the way the economy moves up and down over time. It does not grow at the same pace all the time.
a period when the economy grows strongly. Households spend more, sales rise and businesses hire more workers.
a period when the economy shrinks. Households spend less, sales fall and businesses may cut jobs.
Businesses may need to adjust to both. In a boom they may hire staff or make more stock. In a recession they may cut costs or lower prices to keep customers.
draft.remember: The economy rises and falls, and businesses adjust to both stages.

a.q: Which change is most likely to happen to a business during a recession?
opts: Customers spend less, so sales fall
Customers spend more, so sales rise
Customers buy more, so it hires more staff
Customers stay the same, so nothing changes
a.why: In a recession households spend less, so sales fall. Rising sales and more hiring are signs of a boom, which is the opposite stage.
a.clue: Think about what households do with their money when the economy shrinks.

b.q: Jess owns a bakery in Orange. The economy is in a boom, and orders have risen sharply. What is a sensible way for Jess to adjust?
opts: Hire extra staff to meet the higher demand
Lay off staff to cut costs straight away
Cut prices to attract customers who are scarce
Make less stock so that less is wasted
b.why: In a boom sales and jobs grow, so more demand can mean hiring more staff to meet it. Cutting jobs or prices suits a recession, when customers spend less.
b.clue: Is demand for her bread rising or falling?

a.best: Customers spend less, so sales fall

b.best: Hire extra staff to meet the higher demand
